# Benchmarks

<!-- Generated by `mx r7rs-bench-report`: don't edit by hand. -->

ecraven's R7RS benchmarks (`bench/r7rs-ecraven/`, the set behind <https://ecraven.github.io/r7rs-benchmarks/>) on this implementation and on the other R7RS implementations in `nix develop .#bench`, each run with its own prelude and postlude and as ecraven's `bench` script runs it, so the numbers compare with his tables. How to run it, and what is measured: `bench/README.md`.

## Conditions

- Run by `mx r7rs-bench-report --scale 0.1 --jit-iterations 3 --interpreter-timeout 60 --note 'Noisy numbers: a shared 16-core machine, with other agents building and running benchmarks throughout (load average 10 to 20). Regenerate on a quiet machine, with the programs'"'"' own counts, before relying on differences under 2x.'`, at commit `7eb37798fc2d`, from 2026-11-16 05:34 UTC, for 104.5 minutes.
- Host: Darwin 27.0.0 (arm64), Apple M3 Max, 16 CPUs, 128 GB of memory.
- Noisy numbers: a shared 16-core machine, with other agents building and running benchmarks throughout (load average 10 to 20). Regenerate on a quiet machine, with the programs' own counts, before relying on differences under 2x.
- Counts: 0.1 times each program's own count (at least 1), on every implementation; the Count column gives it.
- Ours, interpreter: run 0.1 times that count (at least 1), its time then scaled up to the count the others ran, marked †.
- Ours, JIT: one JVM runs the harness 3 times. The first, in a fresh process, is the comparable number (as for every other implementation, and in ecraven's tables: the harness's own timing, startup excluded); "JIT steady" is the best of the others, once the JIT has compiled the program.
- A run is killed after 300 s (ecraven's `CPU_LIMIT`), our JIT's after that once per iteration, our interpreter's after 60 s. Peak memory is the process's maximum resident set size. Our JVMs run with the default heap limits (no `-Xmx`), so theirs is as much as the JVM's default ergonomics let the heap grow.

| equal | Guile | timeout (300 s) | `Running equal:10:100:8:1000:2000:5000` |

## How each implementation ran

`{src}` is the program as the bench script builds it, `{input}` its `.input` file (with the count above).

- Ours, JIT: `java (Graal JIT, background compilation) -m scheme.launcher/scheme.launcher.SchemeMain {src} < {input}`. With `bench/postlude.scm` as the postlude.
- Ours, interpreter: `java -Dpolyglot.engine.AllowExperimentalOptions=true -Dpolyglot.engine.Compilation=false -m scheme.launcher/scheme.launcher.SchemeMain {src} < {input}`. With `bench/postlude.scm` as the postlude.
- Chez: `scheme --optimize-level 2 --compile-imported-libraries --libdirs {chezlibs} --program {src} < {input}`. With `Chez-postlude.scm`; ecraven/chez-scheme-libraries, patched: base.sls: vector-append vector-copy!.
- Racket: `raco make {src} && racket {src} < {input}`. With `Racket-prelude.scm`; the r7rs package (lexi-lambda/racket-r7rs, r7rs-lib).
- Chicken: `csc -R r7rs -X r7rs -block -O3 -C -O3 -d0 {src} -o {exe} && {exe} < {input}`. With `Chicken-prelude.scm`.
- Guile: `guild compile -O3 {src} && guile {src} < {input}`. With `Guile-prelude.scm`.
- Gauche: `gosh -r7 -b {src} < {input}`. With `Gauche-postlude.scm`; SLIB 3b7.
- Chibi: `chibi-scheme -m scheme.load -e (load "{src}") < {input}`. With `Chibi-prelude.scm` and `Chibi-postlude.scm`.
